Hi Alice — great to see the diagram, thanks for sending. Below is a focused tenant enablement and ops readiness checklist you can use to prepare your cloud and security teams. I kept it action-oriented so you can hand items off to engineers. Happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk through these.

Redwood tenant enablement & pre-activation checklist (concise):
1) Account & IAM setup
   - Create a tenant service account for the Redwood agent (principal: redwood-agent@helpspring-project) with the minimum roles: compute.networkViewer, dns.admin, storage.objectViewer, logging.logWriter. (We will provide exact IAM JSON on request.)
   - Create one admin service account for onboarding ops (namespacing as in your access matrix). Provide key material via our secure upload flow.
2) Networking & connectivity
   - Allow outbound HTTPS (443) to our control-plane endpoints: api.redwood.ai (cidr ranges: we will share a short list).
   - NAT/Egress: ensure tenant subnet has NAT to allow KV/cache prefetch and telemetry.
   - Peering/Transit: if using VPC peering, share route tables; if using a transit gateway, add a static route for Redwood tenant prefix.
   - Required ports to/from our runtime nodes: 443 (API), 10250 (optional agent health TCP), 50051 (gRPC internal).
3) DNS & TLS
   - Provision internal DNS entry for the tenant's control endpoint; or provide a wildcard cert and CN mapping if preferring mTLS.
   - Certificate requirements: 2048-bit RSA or ECDSA P-256, chain in PEM. We support customer-managed certs and ACM/Cloud KMS integrations.
4) KMS & secrets
   - If you require CMK: create a KMS key with decrypt/encrypt for redwood-agent principal. Provide ARN and rotation policy.
   - We support HSM-backed keys via the KMS provider in your region; if you need proof, we’ll share the integration checklist.
5) Firewall & egress allowlist
   - Provide the public egress IP(s) you expect to use for API callbacks; Redwood will whitelist and provide an optional static egress range under dedicated plans.
6) Monitoring & audit evidence
   - Enable audit logging for storage/compute changes and share a Cloud Logging Read access role to redwood-monitoring@redwood.ai for validation.
   - For pre-activation evidence: collect 3-min packet captures of TLS handshakes (redacted), DNS resolution checks, and a sample API request/response (headers only).
7) Smoke tests we will run together (you run first, then we verify)
   - Authentication: token exchange + KMS decrypt roundtrip.
   - Echo request: post sample payload through tenancy endpoint and compare token latencies.
   - KV cache warmup: send 100 small requests to validate prefix caching and observe metrics.
8) Cutover & rollback plan
   - Define canary window (recommended 1 hour) and monitoring thresholds (error rate > 2% or P50 latency > Xms).
   - Provide a rollback contact list and a DNS TTL you can reduce during cutover.

Deliverables we will provide:
- Exact IP ranges and FQDNs to allowlist (before our scheduled validation)
- A short onboarding runbook (PDF) with step-by-step commands (we will populate with your ARNs and DNS names)
- Test harness config snippet (redwood-reqs-smoke-test-config.txt)

Next steps: can you confirm a 30-min window tomorrow (Wed May 21) for a network deep-dive? Also confirm whether you plan to use customer-managed KMS.

Thanks — Priya
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
